                    ### Question
                    An investigator is studying the structural characteristics of pathogenic viruses. Cell cultures infected by different viruses are observed under a scanning electron microscope. One of the cell samples is infected by a virus that has an envelope composed of nuclear membrane molecules. The most likely virus that has infected this cell sample can cause which of the following conditions?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Yellow fever
opb. Shingles
opc. Erythema infectiosum
opd. Ebola
ope. Condylomata acuminata

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The presence of a virus with an envelope composed of nuclear membrane molecules suggests it buds from the nucleus, which is characteristic of certain DNA viruses, particularly those in the Herpesviridae family. Shingles, caused by the reactivation of Varicella-Zoster Virus (a member of Herpesviridae), aligns with this characteristic. The reasoning chains correctly identify the association between nuclear membrane-derived envelopes and latent infections typical of Herpesviruses. Therefore, the most likely virus that has infected the cell sample can cause Shingles.
